record.file_problem: Repository README and file list only; experimental notes and code were not read.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports prompt-injection and role-confusion experiments, but does not test or rely on the residual-stream refusal direction in the claim.
record.gate_note: The README reports harmful-request and exfiltration attack outcomes, but does not measure, remove, or add the claimed refusal direction. Its role probe measures CoTness/Userness, not the harmful-minus-harmless residual direction. Attack results are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The repo reproduces a prompt-injection/role-confusion paper on gpt-oss-20b. It reports attack success rates and a linear role probe (CoTness/Userness), but never computes, ablates, adds or monitors a harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction. Its jailbreak results do not test whether attacks suppress that direction (V3), and its probe measures perceived role, not refusal.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that prompt injection works through role confusion: forged CoT style makes injected text read as the model's own reasoning, and destyling collapses the attack. They also conclude that user-like framing raises standard-injection success, and that a role probe can act as a style-keyed forgery detector with roughly 2% false positives once recalibrated. They say nothing about a refusal direction.
record.recipe_differences: This is a reproduction and defense project for a different prompt-injection paper, not a reproduction of the refusal-direction method. It reports role probes and prompt attacks, not difference-in-means direction ablation or addition.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary with forgery source, role framing, position, and configuration; the README also reports a calibration threshold change and a corrected run configuration.

fits_no_version.finding: Forged analysis-style prompts raise StrongREJECT jailbreak success on gpt-oss-20b (0% raw, 56.9% styled, 3.8% destyled).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In a reasoning model, forged chain-of-thought style in user input bypasses refusal, and stripping the style removes the effect.

fits_no_version.finding: A forged CoT/policy block raises sandboxed .env exfiltration from 0/30 to 7/30.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Forged reasoning/policy text raises agent exfiltration success.

fits_no_version.finding: Standard-injection success tracks probed Userness: user framing 33%, assistant/tool 6%, other 0%; corr +0.60.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Injection success rises when injected text is perceived as coming from the user.

record.problems: Only README and file list were available; the experimental notes and code were not read. The README reports no uncertainty estimates for the listed outcomes. It describes an initial configuration bug that truncated many runs and a correction, and notes that the agent exfiltration setup is a sandboxed mock.
record.rows_left_out: No reported outcomes were left out from the README that directly bear on harmful-request or exfiltration attack behavior. Role-probe, role-confusion-index, position, and detector metrics were omitted because they do not measure the refusal direction or refusal behavior named by the claim.

untested.parts: No difference-in-means direction, ablation, addition or capability check.
CoT-forgery jailbreaks succeed, but no measurement of the refusal direction during the attacks, and no adversarial training against ablation.
No multi-direction or cone analysis of refusal.
The detector flags forged style, not harmful intent, but harm and refusal representations are not separated.
Cross-model table is todo; no direction transfer.
gpt-oss-20b is a reasoning model, but no refusal-direction test is run on it.

record.verdict_notes: Only the README and file list were available. The file list includes notes/scripts on patching and localization (g5_localize, patching.py, notes/07) that might involve activation interventions, but no results from them are reported in the README. These could be checked if the notes become available.

versions.untested_parts: No difference-in-means refusal direction, ablation, addition, refusal outcome after intervention, or general-capability test.
The README reports prompt-injection attacks but does not test whether they suppress the claimed direction, or train against its ablation.
No comparison of one direction with an affine, cone, or multiple-direction account of refusal.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No transfer test of the claimed direction; the cross-model table is listed as todo.
No test of how refusal training affects the existence of a removable direction.
No reasoning-model test of the claimed direction.

tranche.reason: The repo reproduces a prompt-injection/role-confusion paper on gpt-oss-20b. It never computes, ablates, adds or monitors a harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction, and it makes no argument about one. So it neither tests nor uses the claim.

source_check.notes: The text holds only the README and a file list. The notes/ files it cites (13-21) are not included. All rows are prompt-attack ASRs or role-probe outcomes on gpt-oss-20b with no refusal-direction measure, so versions=none and cannot_determine are right. The study offers role confusion as an alternative jailbreak mechanism but does not test V3. The authors_conclusion paraphrase (about 2% FP after recalibration at thr 0.39) matches the README.
